- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 3–7 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; if below, overcorrects upward — apply opposite bias correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is rising, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast; if falling, subtract 0.5–1.5%.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.0–0.8), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
